title: 2009 AMC 10B Problem 24
statement: The keystone arch is an ancient architectural feature. It is composed of congruent isosceles trapezoids fitted together along the non-parallel sides, as shown. The bottom sides of the two end trapezoids are horizontal. In an arch made with \(9\) trapezoids, let \(x\) be the angle measure in degrees of the larger interior angle of the trapezoid. What is \(x?\)

solutions.text:
Adding a mirror image completes the arch into a symmetric closed loop of \(18\) trapezoids. Their inner edges form a regular \(18\)-gon, each interior angle of which is \[ \dfrac{(18-2)\cdot180^\circ}{18}=160^\circ. \]

At each inner vertex, two of the trapezoids’ larger angles \(x\) meet the \(160^\circ\) angle around a full turn: \(x+x+160^\circ=360^\circ,\) so \(x=100.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Reflect the arch to close it into a full loop of \(18\) trapezoids
The inner vertices form a regular \(18\)-gon; use its interior angle
